evidence.source: Digitimes January 2026; Digitimes May 2026; Largan TWSE monthly filings

evidence.claim: Largan is exclusive or dominant supplier of periscope/tetraprism lenses for iPhone — 85-90% of Apple's periscope procurement; only GSEO has broken in as secondary supplier for iPhone 16 Pro
evidence.source: Digitimes supply chain reports; Ming-Chi Kuo analyst notes; 9to5Mac tetraprism patent battle report November 2023

evidence.claim: Largan declined Apple's request to increase variable aperture lens orders for iPhone 18 Pro, citing prioritization of CPO resources — Apple shifted primary variable aperture supply to Sunny Optical (40-50% allocation); Largan retained secondary role by choice
evidence.source: BigGo Finance; WCCFTech; Geeky Gadgets; Fudzilla; May 2026

evidence.claim: CPO/FAU collaboration with TSMC: samples delivered to TSMC for AMD-related project testing; Largan PhotoniCore Technologies subsidiary; mass production 2027-2028
Humanoid robot vision: Largan entered mass production of precision visual recognition lens systems for humanoid service robots in 2025; overseas shipments delayed from 2025 to 2026
Cash position: NT$123.67B (~US$3.9B) as of June 2025 — 34% of market cap in cash; cash per share NT$926; record NT$179.6B buyback authorized December 2025; dividend yield ~3.75%
evidence.source: Financial data aggregators; Taiwan News December 2025; multiple dividend tracking sources

evidence.claim: Valuation: trading at ~13x P/E vs. peer average 45-55x; cash-adjusted core business at ~10x earnings; Goldman Sachs price target NT$3,549 (current ~NT$2,600); stock 55-60% below 2020 peak despite record revenue
evidence.source: Investing.com citing Goldman Sachs; Alpha Spread; JPMorgan PT NT$3,150; Simply Wall St P/E data

evidence.claim: Manufacturing moat: sub-200nm surface accuracy tolerances, 2,700+ patents, 35-year tacit process knowledge, NT$13B+ (>$400M) annual capex 2025 — no competitor has demonstrated equivalent yield at 8P+/variable aperture spec at volume scale
evidence.source: BALD Engineering blog April 2024; 9to5Mac; industry technical analysis; Digitimes capacity reports

what_could_weaken_view: Sunny Optical demonstrates yield parity on variable aperture lenses for iPhone 18 Pro at scale — if Sunny captures 40-50% primary allocation and executes successfully, the premium-spec moat begins to narrow meaningfully beyond the 7P tier

Variable aperture yield issues persist into Q1 2027 — Largan's own disclosures cite yield improvement as a 2026 goal; if H2 2026 production ramp is slower than expected, iPhone 18 Pro camera volumes at risk

Computational photography reduces optical hardware intensity — Apple's investment in AI image processing (ProRes video, computational zoom) could reduce the number of discrete cameras or lens elements required per device in iPhone 19+ cycles
Robot vision shipments delayed again beyond 2026 — first delay was 2025→2026; second delay would signal customer qualification problems or market timing mismatch, not just schedule slip

Taiwan geopolitical escalation — manufacturing concentration in Taichung creates catastrophic single-point risk; no meaningful offshore diversification in place; 2 of 6 factories are in China, creating dual-jurisdiction exposure
CPO/FAU mass production slips to 2028-2029 — TSMC/AMD sampling is real but mass production timeline is management guidance, not contracted; AI infrastructure procurement cycles are unpredictable
